item.content:encoded:
+1 because it made me laugh. Driving an hour to and from work, I saw myself represented here perfectly. Everyone is a terrible driver except me!

As for improving it…I don't know, really. I like that it's short, escalates nicely, and ends with the wreck and the footnote. And I think the incident logs did a pretty good job in showing that he's obsessing over really minor bad driving habits that we all do. Re-writing it so he's constantly at fault instead of just raging out over imaginary slights seems like it would detract from the joke.

I guess if I had to throw out an idea, maybe an interview with Dr. Estevez exploring the idea of how the "SCP" made him drive like a moron? Problem is the longer the article goes, the quicker the joke will get stale. I honestly think it's fine as is.

If that was what you were going for, it might be clearer if one of the incident logs is an event where he's clearly the party in the wrong, but blames it on the other guy anyway because of course all of his behavior has a rational explanation and is perfectly understandable given his circumstances and it's the other guy's fault for not taking these clearly common and understandable situations into account. He was in a hurry, he was distracted by something, he didn't notice the other car, blah blah blah. Because when HE screws up, it's because of external factors, but when anyone else screws up, it's because they are screwups.
